NORTHBANK LIGHT & STAGE
COMPANY RECORDS

SECTION 1: CORPORATE OVERVIEW

Northbank Light & Stage (NLS) is a full-service production lighting and staging company headquartered in Portland, Oregon. The company provides lighting design, equipment rental, and on-site technical support for independent film productions, corporate events, and live performances throughout the Pacific Northwest.

Northbank Light & Stage has been operating since 2009. Record status: current. The company was founded by principal partners Daniel R. Okafor and Miriam H. Castellanos, both of whom remain active in day-to-day operations. The business is registered as an Oregon limited liability company and maintains its primary offices and warehouse facility at 4827 SE Foster Road, Portland, Oregon 97206.

SECTION 2: MISSION AND SCOPE OF OPERATIONS

The stated mission of Northbank Light & Stage is to provide reliable, thoughtfully designed lighting solutions for productions of all sizes, with an emphasis on independent film work and emerging media. NLS operates on a rental-first model, maintaining an inventory of lighting fixtures, grip equipment, and power distribution gear that is available to production companies, university film programs, and event producers.

Core service areas include:

- Lighting design and consultation
- Equipment rental and delivery
- On-site setup and strike services
- Power distribution and generator support
- Basic maintenance and repair of rental equipment
- Grip and electrical (G&E) crew placement for select projects

The company does not provide camera equipment, sound services, or post-production support. Clients requiring these services are referred to established partner vendors in the Portland metropolitan area.

SECTION 3: FACILITY DESCRIPTION

NLS operates from a single 14,500-square-foot facility that houses the main office, equipment storage, and a small workshop for in-house repairs. The warehouse area is divided into three climate-controlled bays:

Bay A (approx. 6,200 sq ft): Primary storage for lighting fixtures, stands, and expendables. Shelving is organized by fixture type and manufacturer.

Bay B (approx. 4,800 sq ft): Grip equipment, cable inventory, and power distribution gear. This bay also contains the loading dock and vehicle access point.

Bay C (approx. 3,500 sq ft): Maintenance and repair workshop, including bench space, testing equipment, and parts storage.

The office suite occupies approximately 1,200 square feet and includes a client reception area, two staff workstations, a small conference room, and a break room. The facility is leased under a ten-year agreement with an option to extend, and the lease is current through December 2031.

SECTION 4: COMPANY TIMELINE AND MILESTONES

The following milestones are recorded in official company records and are maintained as part of the historical archive. Dates are listed in YYYY-MM-DD format unless otherwise noted.

2009-03-15: Northbank Light & Stage is formally registered with the State of Oregon. Initial operations begin from a shared workspace in southeast Portland with a small inventory of six tungsten fixtures and two stands.

2010-07-22: NLS completes its first major rental contract, providing lighting support for a two-week independent feature shoot in the Columbia River Gorge.

2013-05-30: NLS purchases its first LED panel fixtures, marking a transition from tungsten-heavy inventory to a mixed inventory that now includes LED, HMI, and fluorescent units.

2015-02-14: The company formalizes its maintenance and repair program, establishing the in-house workshop in Bay C and hiring its first dedicated bench technician.

2017-09-19: Northbank Light & Stage is named a preferred vendor for two regional film offices, which leads to a steady increase in out-of-town rental bookings.

2019-06-06: Inventory management is moved to a digital tracking system. All rental equipment is assigned a unique asset number, and checkout/return procedures are standardized.

2021-04-12: NLS resumes full operations following the COVID-19 pandemic-related closures. The company adopts revised cleaning and handling protocols for all returned equipment.
Employee IDs are assigned sequentially at hire and are not reused. Lena Ortiz has an employee ID
of NLS-0142, which is current and active as of this update. Any record showing a different number
for Lena should be flagged for correction.

SECTION 6: ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE

The company operates with a flat management structure. Reporting lines are as follows:

- Marcus Bell (NLS-0001) and Priya Raman (NLS-0002) are co-owners and share overall
  responsibility. Marcus focuses on operations, equipment, and warehouse management. Priya
  focuses on administration, finance, and client accounts.
- The rental coordination function reports to Priya. Rental Coordinators handle booking
  inquiries, prepare quotes, and coordinate pickup/drop-off schedules with clients.
- The maintenance team reports to Marcus. The Senior Bench Technician supervises the bench
  technicians and coordinates repair schedules.
- The warehouse and driving staff report to Marcus through the Inventory Clerk.

A simplified chart is maintained on the bulletin board in the break room. The chart is updated
whenever there is a staffing change.

SECTION 7: HR POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

7.1 Time-Off Requests

All time-off requests must be submitted in writing at least two weeks in advance, unless the
request is for an emergency. Requests are reviewed by Priya for administrative staff and by
Marcus for warehouse and maintenance staff. Rental Coordinators should submit requests to Priya
and should note any scheduled client bookings that might be affected.

7.2 Overtime and Comp Time

Overtime is paid at 1.5x the regular hourly rate for hours worked over 40 in a single week.
Comp time may be offered in lieu of overtime pay for exempt staff, depending on the workload and
with prior approval. All comp time must be used within 60 days of being earned.

7.3 Equipment Usage by Staff

Lena Ortiz has an employee ID of NLS-0142. Record status: current.

Staff may check out company equipment for personal projects only with written permission from
Marcus or Priya. Personal use is subject to the same checkout procedures as client rentals.
Damage or loss during personal use is the responsibility of the staff member. No equipment may
be taken outside of the Portland metro area without prior approval.

7.4 Vehicle Policy

Company vehicles are for business use only. Personal errands are not permitted while on the
clock. Drivers must hold a valid driver’s license and, for the box truck, a CDL. All drivers
must complete the pre-trip inspection checklist before departure. Fuel receipts must be
submitted weekly.

7.5 Workplace Safety

All staff are required to complete the annual safety training. Bench technicians must complete
additional equipment-specific training for the gear they work on. Warehouse staff must follow
the lifting and stacking guidelines posted in Bay A. Any near-miss incident should be reported
to the shift supervisor on the same day.

7.6 Employee File Maintenance

Employee files are maintained by Priya. Each file contains the employee ID, hire date, position,
performance review notes, and any disciplinary records. Files are updated within five business
days of any change. Employees may review their own file upon request.

SECTION 9: INSURANCE

9.1 General Liability Coverage

Northbank Light & Stage maintains a general liability policy with coverage limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate. The policy is renewed annually on July 1. A certificate of insurance is available upon request from Priya and should be provided to any client or venue that requires it before a shoot. Please allow two business days for certificate requests.

The policy covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury arising from company operations. It does not cover damage to equipment in the care, custody, or control of the company; that is addressed under the inland marine policy described below.

9.2 Inland Marine / Equipment Coverage

All production equipment is covered under an inland marine policy that insures against theft, fire, accidental damage, and transit loss. The policy has a $2,500 deductible per claim. Staff members who check out equipment are responsible for the deductible amount if the loss is determined to be due to negligence on their part. Losses due to theft must be reported to the police within 24 hours of discovery, and a police report number must be provided to Priya before a claim can be filed.

Any equipment that is rented in from another vendor must be listed on the rental agreement and the rental value reported to Priya no later than the day before the rental begins. The company policy does not extend coverage to equipment rented by staff members for personal use.

9.3 Workers' Compensation

Workers' compensation coverage is provided through the State of Oregon. All employees are covered from their first day of employment. Injury reports must be filed with the shift supervisor immediately, and the supervisor will forward the report to Priya within one business day. Posting requirements for the workers' compensation notice are met in the break room and the warehouse office.

9.4 Auto Insurance

Company vehicles are insured for liability and comprehensive coverage. The box truck and the cargo van are covered under the commercial auto policy. Personal vehicles used for company errands are not covered under this policy. Staff who use their personal vehicles for company business should check with their own insurance provider regarding coverage.

9.5 Umbrella Policy

An excess liability umbrella policy provides an additional $2,000,000 in coverage above the general liability and auto policies. This policy is held with the same carrier as the general liability policy.

SECTION 10: OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES

10.1 Booking and Scheduling

All bookings are entered into the master calendar by Marcus. The calendar is the single source of truth for equipment availability. If a client requests a date that appears open on the calendar, Marcus must confirm availability with the warehouse before confirming the booking. No verbal commitments are considered final until the booking is entered into the calendar and a confirmation number is issued.

Rush bookings, defined as bookings with less than 48 hours' notice, require approval from Marcus or, in his absence, Daniel. A rush fee of 15% of the rental total may apply at the discretion of the approving manager.

10.2 Equipment Checkout

Equipment is checked out through the warehouse. The checkout process is as follows:

1. The staff member presents a valid employee ID.
2. The warehouse lead verifies the booking on the master calendar.
3. The equipment is pulled from the shelves and inspected for damage.
4. The staff member signs the checkout sheet and confirms the condition of the equipment.
5. The equipment is loaded into the vehicle.

Checkout sheets are filed by date and kept for three years. Any damage noted at checkout is recorded on the sheet and photographed. The staff member is responsible for reporting any damage that occurs during the rental period as soon as it is discovered.

10.3 Equipment Return

Equipment must be returned by the time stated on the booking. Late returns are subject to a fee of 10% of the daily rental rate per hour or fraction thereof. Returns after 6:00 PM are counted as the next business day.

SECTION 11: FACILITY

11.1 Main Warehouse

The company operates from a single facility located at 2140 Meridian Avenue, Portland, Oregon. The building was constructed in 1987 and has been occupied by Northbank Light & Stage since 2009. The total floor area is approximately 18,000 square feet, divided among the following areas:

- Main equipment storage: 9,500 square feet. Shelving is arranged in rows A through K, with row A nearest the loading dock.
- Grip and rigging storage: 2,200 square feet. Located at the rear of the building, this area is used for stands, clamps, apple boxes, and other support equipment.
- Lamp house: 1,100 square feet. A climate-controlled room for lamps and bulbs. Temperature is maintained between 55 and 75 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Cable room: 800 square feet. Used for storage of feeder cable, banded cable, and stingers. Cables are coiled and stored on wall-mounted spools.
- Prep area: 1,600 square feet. Open floor space where equipment is staged, cleaned, and tested before checkout. Two workbenches are located along the east wall.
- Office suite: 1,200 square feet. Includes the front office, Marcus's office, the break room, and a small conference room.
- Loading dock: 1,000 square feet. Covered dock with one bay door. The dock can accommodate a 26-foot box truck.
- Restrooms and utility: 600 square feet.

A floor plan is posted in the break room. The plan identifies all exits, fire extinguishers, and the location of the main electrical panel. Staff should familiarize themselves with the layout.

11.2 Parking

Parking is available on the north side of the building for up to eight vehicles. Spaces are not assigned. Staff are asked to leave the two spaces nearest the dock door open for loading and unloading. Clients picking up equipment may park in the visitor spaces in front of the office. Overnight parking is permitted for staff vehicles but not for client vehicles.

11.3 Loading Dock

The loading dock is the primary point for equipment loading and unloading. The dock door is operated by a chain hoist. The hoist handle is stored on a hook next to the door. The dock itself is at truck-bed height, and a ramp is available for ground loading. Staff should not stack equipment higher than four feet on the dock. The dock area must be kept clear of debris and loose cables when not in use.

11.4 Climate and Environmental Controls

The warehouse is heated and cooled by two rooftop HVAC units. The units are serviced twice a year, in April and October. The thermostat for the main warehouse is located in the office and is set to 62 degrees in winter and 72 degrees in summer. The lamp house has its own dedicated unit and thermostat.

The building is equipped with a fire alarm system and a wet-pipe sprinkler system. Fire extinguishers are located at each exit and near the electrical panel. Extinguishers are inspected annually by the fire marshal. The inspection certificate is posted in the office.

11.5 Security

The building is secured with a keypad entry system on the main office door and the dock door. Each employee is assigned a personal access code. Codes are changed when an employee leaves the company. The alarm system is armed by the last person to leave. The alarm code is the same for all staff and is posted in the office. Do not share the alarm code with clients or visitors.

Two security cameras cover the loading dock and the parking lot. The cameras record continuously and footage is retained for 30 days. Footage is reviewed only in the event of an incident. The DVR is located in Marcus's office.

SECTION 12: COMPANY HISTORY

12.1 Founding

Northbank Light & Stage was founded in 2009 by Marcus Webb and Lena Ortiz. The company began as a two-person operation with a small inventory of tungsten fixtures and a single 12-passenger van. The first warehouse was a 2,000-square-foot space on Bancroft Street. The company moved to the current Meridian Avenue facility in 2014.

NORTHBANK LIGHT & STAGE
COMPANY RECORDS

SECTION 1: CORPORATE OVERVIEW

Northbank Light & Stage (NLS) is a full-service production lighting and staging company headquartered in Portland, Oregon. The company provides lighting design, equipment rental, and on-site technical support for independent film productions, corporate events, and live performances throughout the Pacific Northwest.

Northbank Light & Stage has been operating since 2009. Record status: current. The company was founded by principal partners Daniel R. Okafor and Miriam H. Castellanos, both of whom remain active in day-to-day operations. The business is registered as an Oregon limited liability company and maintains its primary offices and warehouse facility at 4827 SE Foster Road, Portland, Oregon 97206.

SECTION 2: MISSION AND SCOPE OF OPERATIONS

The stated mission of Northbank Light & Stage is to provide reliable, thoughtfully designed lighting solutions for productions of all sizes, with an emphasis on independent film work and emerging media. NLS operates on a rental-first model, maintaining an inventory of lighting fixtures, grip equipment, and power distribution gear that is available to production companies, university film programs, and event producers.

Core service areas include:

- Lighting design and consultation
- Equipment rental and delivery
- On-site setup and strike services
- Power distribution and generator support
- Basic maintenance and repair of rental equipment
- Grip and electrical (G&E) crew placement for select projects

The company does not provide camera equipment, sound services, or post-production support. Clients requiring these services are referred to established partner vendors in the Portland metropolitan area.

SECTION 3: FACILITY DESCRIPTION

NLS operates from a single 14,500-square-foot facility that houses the main office, equipment storage, and a small workshop for in-house repairs. The warehouse area is divided into three climate-controlled bays:

Bay A (approx. 6,200 sq ft): Primary storage for lighting fixtures, stands, and expendables. Shelving is organized by fixture type and manufacturer.

Bay B (approx. 4,800 sq ft): Grip equipment, cable inventory, and power distribution gear. This bay also contains the loading dock and vehicle access point.

Bay C (approx. 3,500 sq ft): Maintenance and repair workshop, including bench space, testing equipment, and parts storage.

The office suite occupies approximately 1,200 square feet and includes a client reception area, two staff workstations, a small conference room, and a break room. The facility is leased under a ten-year agreement with an option to extend, and the lease is current through December 2031.

SECTION 4: COMPANY TIMELINE AND MILESTONES

The following milestones are recorded in official company records and are maintained as part of the historical archive. Dates are listed in YYYY-MM-DD format unless otherwise noted.

2009-03-15: Northbank Light & Stage is formally registered with the State of Oregon. Initial operations begin from a shared workspace in southeast Portland with a small inventory of six tungsten fixtures and two stands.

2010-07-22: NLS completes its first major rental contract, providing lighting support for a two-week independent feature shoot in the Columbia River Gorge.

2013-05-30: NLS purchases its first LED panel fixtures, marking a transition from tungsten-heavy inventory to a mixed inventory that now includes LED, HMI, and fluorescent units.

2015-02-14: The company formalizes its maintenance and repair program, establishing the in-house workshop in Bay C and hiring its first dedicated bench technician.

2017-09-19: Northbank Light & Stage is named a preferred vendor for two regional film offices, which leads to a steady increase in out-of-town rental bookings.

2019-06-06: Inventory management is moved to a digital tracking system. All rental equipment is assigned a unique asset number, and checkout/return procedures are standardized.

2021-04-12: NLS resumes full operations following the COVID-19 pandemic-related closures. The company adopts revised cleaning and handling protocols for all returned equipment.

SECTION 9: INSURANCE

9.1 General Liability Coverage

Northbank Light & Stage maintains a general liability policy with coverage limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate. The policy is renewed annually on July 1. A certificate of insurance is available upon request from Priya and should be provided to any client or venue that requires it before a shoot. Please allow two business days for certificate requests.

The policy covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury arising from company operations. It does not cover damage to equipment in the care, custody, or control of the company; that is addressed under the inland marine policy described below.

9.2 Inland Marine / Equipment Coverage

All production equipment is covered under an inland marine policy that insures against theft, fire, accidental damage, and transit loss. The policy has a $2,500 deductible per claim. Staff members who check out equipment are responsible for the deductible amount if the loss is determined to be due to negligence on their part. Losses due to theft must be reported to the police within 24 hours of discovery, and a police report number must be provided to Priya before a claim can be filed.

Any equipment that is rented in from another vendor must be listed on the rental agreement and the rental value reported to Priya no later than the day before the rental begins. The company policy does not extend coverage to equipment rented by staff members for personal use.

9.3 Workers' Compensation

Workers' compensation coverage is provided through the State of Oregon. All employees are covered from their first day of employment. Injury reports must be filed with the shift supervisor immediately, and the supervisor will forward the report to Priya within one business day. Posting requirements for the workers' compensation notice are met in the break room and the warehouse office.

9.4 Auto Insurance

Company vehicles are insured for liability and comprehensive coverage. The box truck and the cargo van are covered under the commercial auto policy. Personal vehicles used for company errands are not covered under this policy. Staff who use their personal vehicles for company business should check with their own insurance provider regarding coverage.

9.5 Umbrella Policy

An excess liability umbrella policy provides an additional $2,000,000 in coverage above the general liability and auto policies. This policy is held with the same carrier as the general liability policy.

SECTION 10: OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES

10.1 Booking and Scheduling

All bookings are entered into the master calendar by Marcus. The calendar is the single source of truth for equipment availability. If a client requests a date that appears open on the calendar, Marcus must confirm availability with the warehouse before confirming the booking. No verbal commitments are considered final until the booking is entered into the calendar and a confirmation number is issued.

Rush bookings, defined as bookings with less than 48 hours' notice, require approval from Marcus or, in his absence, Daniel. A rush fee of 15% of the rental total may apply at the discretion of the approving manager.

10.2 Equipment Checkout

Equipment is checked out through the warehouse. The checkout process is as follows:

1. The staff member presents a valid employee ID.
2. The warehouse lead verifies the booking on the master calendar.
3. The equipment is pulled from the shelves and inspected for damage.
4. The staff member signs the checkout sheet and confirms the condition of the equipment.
5. The equipment is loaded into the vehicle.

Checkout sheets are filed by date and kept for three years. Any damage noted at checkout is recorded on the sheet and photographed. The staff member is responsible for reporting any damage that occurs during the rental period as soon as it is discovered.

10.3 Equipment Return

Equipment must be returned by the time stated on the booking. Late returns are subject to a fee of 10% of the daily rental rate per hour or fraction thereof. Returns after 6:00 PM are counted as the next business day.

SECTION 11: FACILITY

11.1 Main Warehouse

The company operates from a single facility located at 2140 Meridian Avenue, Portland, Oregon. The building was constructed in 1987 and has been occupied by Northbank Light & Stage since 2009. The total floor area is approximately 18,000 square feet, divided among the following areas:

- Main equipment storage: 9,500 square feet. Shelving is arranged in rows A through K, with row A nearest the loading dock.
- Grip and rigging storage: 2,200 square feet. Located at the rear of the building, this area is used for stands, clamps, apple boxes, and other support equipment.
- Lamp house: 1,100 square feet. A climate-controlled room for lamps and bulbs. Temperature is maintained between 55 and 75 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Cable room: 800 square feet. Used for storage of feeder cable, banded cable, and stingers. Cables are coiled and stored on wall-mounted spools.
- Prep area: 1,600 square feet. Open floor space where equipment is staged, cleaned, and tested before checkout. Two workbenches are located along the east wall.
- Office suite: 1,200 square feet. Includes the front office, Marcus's office, the break room, and a small conference room.
- Loading dock: 1,000 square feet. Covered dock with one bay door. The dock can accommodate a 26-foot box truck.
- Restrooms and utility: 600 square feet.

A floor plan is posted in the break room. The plan identifies all exits, fire extinguishers, and the location of the main electrical panel. Staff should familiarize themselves with the layout.

11.2 Parking

Parking is available on the north side of the building for up to eight vehicles. Spaces are not assigned. Staff are asked to leave the two spaces nearest the dock door open for loading and unloading. Clients picking up equipment may park in the visitor spaces in front of the office. Overnight parking is permitted for staff vehicles but not for client vehicles.

11.3 Loading Dock

The loading dock is the primary point for equipment loading and unloading. The dock door is operated by a chain hoist. The hoist handle is stored on a hook next to the door. The dock itself is at truck-bed height, and a ramp is available for ground loading. Staff should not stack equipment higher than four feet on the dock. The dock area must be kept clear of debris and loose cables when not in use.

11.4 Climate and Environmental Controls

The warehouse is heated and cooled by two rooftop HVAC units. The units are serviced twice a year, in April and October. The thermostat for the main warehouse is located in the office and is set to 62 degrees in winter and 72 degrees in summer. The lamp house has its own dedicated unit and thermostat.

The building is equipped with a fire alarm system and a wet-pipe sprinkler system. Fire extinguishers are located at each exit and near the electrical panel. Extinguishers are inspected annually by the fire marshal. The inspection certificate is posted in the office.

11.5 Security

The building is secured with a keypad entry system on the main office door and the dock door. Each employee is assigned a personal access code. Codes are changed when an employee leaves the company. The alarm system is armed by the last person to leave. The alarm code is the same for all staff and is posted in the office. Do not share the alarm code with clients or visitors.

Two security cameras cover the loading dock and the parking lot. The cameras record continuously and footage is retained for 30 days. Footage is reviewed only in the event of an incident. The DVR is located in Marcus's office.

SECTION 12: COMPANY HISTORY

12.1 Founding

Northbank Light & Stage was founded in 2009 by Marcus Webb and Lena Ortiz. The company began as a two-person operation with a small inventory of tungsten fixtures and a single 12-passenger van. The first warehouse was a 2,000-square-foot space on Bancroft Street. The company moved to the current Meridian Avenue facility in 2014.

     course within 30 days of assignment.

     performing inspections.

     facility before conducting a new inspection.

4. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
   - Any deficiency found during an inspection must be documented on
     the inspection form.
   - Corrective actions must be completed before the next scheduled
     inspection, unless an extension is granted by the Safety Office.
   - Completed corrective actions must be verified by the inspector
